newsitem.title: CHINA: China says to pipe water to Taiwan-run island.
newsitem.headline: China says to pipe water to Taiwan-run island.

text.p: China has renewed an offer to supply water to parched islands controlled by arch-rival Taiwan and plans to build a pipe to one of the islands within two years, the Xinhua news agency said on Sunday.

Authorities in Xiamen city in China's eastern Fujian province were ready to start quenching the thirst of residents of Taiwan-controlled Quemoy (Jinmen) Island at any time, Xinhua quoted Xiamen tap water company manager Ye Yinghui as saying.
Water could be supplied to Quemoy either by ship or by pipeline, with a flow of up to 1,000 tonnes a day presenting now problems for mainland water authorities, Ye said.
"A pipeline between Xiamen and Quemoy will be laid within two years," the official agency quoted him as saying but gave no details.

Taiwan, Beijing's bitter rival since becoming the refuge of the defeated Nationalist government in 1949 at the end of a long-fought civil war, in July said it planned to import water from China for Quemoy and another frontline island, Matsu.
Both islands suffer severe water shortages, estimated at 800 tonnes of water a day in Quemoy and 600 tonnes a day in Matsu.
Chinese officials have repeatedly offered to supply water to the heavily-militarised islands, which lie just off the mainlands coast, but have said Taipei is wary of accepting.
Beijing has considered Taiwan a rebel province since 1949 and has threatened to invade if the island ever declares formal independence.

China conducted a series of intimidatory military exercises and missile tests in the waters near Taiwan during the island's first direct presidential elections last March, but tensions across the narrow Taiwan Strait have subsided in recent months.
